title: Cycle time and lead time, and where the waiting actually happens

videos.script: Here is one item from the Billing team's board, a bug called BIL-153. It was reported on the twenty-fourth of June. {{item}} Somebody started it on the ninth of July. It merged on the fifth of August, and it reached production that evening. {{dates}} So how long did it take? Twenty-seven days, if you ask the developer. Forty-two, if you ask the shop owner who reported it. {{two}} Both answers are right. They read two different clocks. {{clocks}} This lesson names the two clocks. Then it measures the spread around them, because an average hides the items that hurt. {{spread}} Then it takes the lead time apart, column by column, to find where the days went. {{columns}} The answer is rarely the work. It is the waiting. {{waiting}}
